name: Verizon Business

profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Hillsboro, Oregon carries the name Verizon Hillsboro Tanasbourne Data Center with operator tagged as Verizon Business. Hillsboro is a well-established data center market in the Portland metro area, and third-party colocation directories list roughly forty five distinct operators active there, none of which this research identified as Verizon-operated commercial space, which is a signal against this being an active colocation facility open to outside tenants. Verizon prior data center footprint traces mainly to its 2011 acquisition of Terremark, a colocation and cloud provider, but Verizon divested that Terremark-descended commercial data center business twice: first selling a set of European and Latin American data centers to Equinix in a roughly 3.5 billion dollar deal announced in late 2016 and closed in 2017 covering 29 data centers across 15 markets, and separately selling its remaining Terremark-branded US cloud and colocation operations to IBM around May 2017. Equinix current published footprint does not include an Oregon market, and the Equinix 2017 acquisition list does not appear to have included any Pacific Northwest facility, so this Hillsboro building does not match the known Equinix-acquired set. It is possible this record reflects a legacy or since-repurposed Verizon or Terremark-era facility, stale OSM tagging carried over from an earlier company presence, or genuine but undocumented current Verizon Business network infrastructure. Oregon sits outside Verizon nine-state incumbent local exchange carrier territory, which weighs against a legacy regional Bell explanation. No operator fact sheet, county assessor record, or trade-press source confirming an active Verizon-operated facility at this address was found this session. Given the ambiguity, this record is presented as an honest open question rather than a confirmed operating data center, and no capacity, square footage, tier, or year-built figures are asserted.

sources.title: Equinix to Acquire 29 Data Centers from Verizon

profile.research_note: Verizon exited the commercial colocation business in 2017 (sold 29 IBX facilities to Equinix); no current verizon.com/business page publishes a dedicated data-center spec sheet for the Hillsboro/Tanasbourne location -- only generic store/service locators found. Treated as genuinely unpublished.

reading:
Verizon Business is the enterprise arm of Verizon Communications, and the single facility recorded under it here is a building in Hillsboro, Oregon, at 9450 Northeast Tanasbourne Drive, inside the Tanasbourne Corporate Center. Whether it is a data centre at all is the open question, and the map record shows exactly where the claim came from.

The building was drawn in March 2015 with nothing on it but a generic building tag. In July 2022 a contributor named it Verizon, set the operator to Verizon and classified it as a telecom exchange, which is the tag for a telephone central office. It stayed that way through a further edit in December 2025. On 20 April 2026 one contributor changed the classification from exchange to data centre, changed the building tag from generic to industrial and set the operator to Verizon Business, then in a second changeset the same evening renamed it from Verizon to Verizon Hillsboro Tanasbourne Data Center. The name that reads like an official facility designation was written by a mapper, not by Verizon, and the reclassification from switching centre to data centre rests on that single evening of edits.

Verizon publishes nothing about a Hillsboro data centre. There is no site page, no capacity, no square footage, no IT load, no utility service size and no standby generator count, nothing that would let anyone outside the company decide whether the building holds switching and transport equipment or hosting floor.

The reclassification matters because Verizon largely left the colocation business. Equinix acquired a portfolio of 29 Verizon data centres in the United States and Latin America for 3.6 billion dollars, a transaction Equinix described in its first quarter 2017 results filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission and completed later that year. Any building still carrying a Verizon colocation label is therefore a candidate for stale attribution unless the current operator is confirmed directly, and this one has not been.

Hillsboro is one of the larger data centre clusters in the Pacific Northwest, and this registry holds two other operators within a few miles of this building, an Aligned campus and an EdgeConneX site, both of which publish site pages naming their buildings and giving at least floor areas. This one does not, and that absence is itself the finding. On the evidence available, the defensible description is a Verizon telecommunications building in Tanasbourne whose classification as a data centre rests on a single 2026 map edit, and the registry should not carry a capacity figure for it.
